text: You're at the supermarket, a stick-figure on a mission. Your cart empty, your focus narrow. You just need milk.
So you head straight for the back, weaving through aisles of tempting products. Why is it always so far away?
Your naive brain thinks it's about refrigeration or heavy lifting. But the real reason is far more subtle, designed for you.
Milk, bread, eggs — these are 'destination' items. Supermarkets place them at farthest points to maximize your exposure.
Every step past snacks, drinks, and impulse buys is an opportunity for you to add something extra, increasing their profit.
Now you see it. That long walk to the dairy aisle isn't a chore; it's a carefully crafted journey through an invisible sales machine.
